Predators and pests are built around their working parts. The European mantis spends its 20,352 polygons on spined raptorial forelegs, the detail that makes it read as a hunter, with ten maps for chitin, wing veins and compound eyes. The dragonfly's veined wings catch light like stained glass over water, the potato beetle comes in two builds for farming and science content, and the camel spider is offered plain and with fur.

An ant is read by its gait, and a gait is rig work. That is why rigged pieces matter among these Animals & Creatures: a red ant, a swallowtail flapping its wings, a mouse spider with fur and an animated honey bee. The monarch chrysalis needs only 420 polygons. They fit nature documentaries, educational animation, pollination and pest explainers, and garden scenes.

electronics-gadgets/smartphones.lead: Smartphones inside and out: recent and earlier flagship handsets, generic phones for app mockups and sets in several colors. The section also has an unusual depth of technical models, including fully disassembled phones, closed phones with their complete internal structure and a bare logic board. Accessories range from clear and silicone cases to a selfie stick, earbuds and a pocket photo printer.
body: A disassembled phone is a repair manual, a teardown video and a product cutaway in one, but only if the parts are truly separate. In the teardown models the display assembly, battery, logic board, camera module, haptic motor, shields and screws are individual objects. They can be laid flat, exploded along an axis or animated back into the chassis. The closed phones with full internal structure keep those parts in their real positions, so the device looks finished until the housing turns transparent. A bare logic board builds the shields, connector sockets, spring contacts and silkscreen markings at real proportions, not as a stylized green rectangle.

Exterior models cover several generations. A recent pro handset with a brushed frame and a triple camera plateau holds 23,774 polygons, and an early touchscreen phone keeps its curved plastic back and lone home button. A generic large-screen phone with a punch-hole camera is a subdivision model of 13,212 polygons without texture maps, made for app and device mockups. Color sets save time when a scene needs several handsets of the same model.
Accessories are light: a silicone case with a magnet ring needs 4,960 polygons. This is the Electronics & Gadgets corner for repair guides, tech journalism, app store imagery and electronics lessons.

electronics-gadgets/cameras.lead: Cameras for photography, film, broadcast and security: lenses and a mechanical iris, mirrorless and full-frame DSLR bodies, classic 35 mm film and instant cameras. Action cameras, camcorders, a high-speed cinema camera and studio cameras on pedestals follow. Tripods, a rail dolly, a gimbal kit, body cameras and street surveillance cameras on a pole round out the section.
body: A broadcast studio camera is read through its bulk. The generic model of 306,812 polygons keeps the box body, the large lens with its servo controls, the viewfinder, the teleprompter mount and the pan bars. A full-frame mirrorless body shows how removing the mirror shortened cameras and their flange distances, with 29 maps across 59,665 polygons. A compact professional camcorder carries 53 maps for its matte housing, rubber grip and many small printed labels. Lenses work as props on their own: a standard zoom uses six maps for focal markings, rubber texture and coated glass.

History is well covered. A classic 35 mm SLR keeps its winding lever, shutter speed dial and leatherette body. An antique folding plate camera stands on a wooden tripod with pleated bellows and a brass lens. An open instant camera pushes a fresh print out of its slot, and a mechanical iris of overlapping blades doubles as a sci-fi door or a transition graphic.

Security and production gear complete this corner of the Electronics & Gadgets category. A body camera sits on a magnetic mount, and a cluster of street cameras shows weathered paint and warning stickers. A rail dolly carries an operator seat, and a gimbal wears a fluffy wind cover. Film-set and newsroom scenes, photography advertising and smart city visualization get the most from them.

electronics-gadgets/laptops-computers.lead: Laptops and computers from beige classics to current thin notebooks: generic laptops at several levels of detail, pro and ultrabook models, rugged military laptops and field tablets. Retro desktops with tube monitors, a handheld gaming computer and a quantum computer core widen the range. Technical pieces include a laptop with its complete inner structure and a laptop heat sink and fan unit.
body: Generic laptops come at different weights for different jobs. The thin generic laptop stays lean at 21,136 polygons for desk clutter and background use. Another generic model spends 134,265 polygons on individually modeled keycaps, the hinge mechanism, the port cutouts and the display bezel, since the keyboard is the giveaway in an over-the-shoulder office shot. On a 16-inch pro laptop the port layout dates the machine precisely, and CheckMate Pro scale lets it sit correctly on a desk beside a coffee cup and a phone.

Some models open up. A laptop with detailed inner structure hides the logic board, battery cells, cooling fan and keyboard assembly under its shell in 945,446 polygons. A separate cooling unit shows copper heat pipes, a thin fin stack and a blower fan. The quantum computer core takes the familiar chandelier form, stacked gold plates linked by coiled coaxial lines, with each cable built as real geometry.

Retro machines carry their own stories. One is a Japanese personal computer whose text-handling hardware set it apart from western machines. Others are a compact beige all-in-one from the early desktop publishing years and a white school computer with a built-in tube display. Rugged laptops with sealed ports and corner bumpers suit defense scenes. Together they furnish offices, classrooms, tech advertising and period film sets across the Electronics & Gadgets range.

electronics-gadgets/headphones-audio.lead: Personal and room audio: wireless earbuds with their charging cases, and over-ear headphones on stands, desk hooks and mannequin heads. Soundbars with subwoofers, portable and pixel-art speakers, PA cabinets with tripod stands and public address horns cover the room. Tall horn towers suit listening rooms, and a few wearable pairings and a retail earbud box are included.
body: Earbuds are shown with their case, since the case is half of the product's identity. One wireless set of 55,530 polygons uses seven maps for the glossy white plastic, the mesh grilles and the metal contacts, and its CheckMate Pro scale matters on an object this small. Another set is built from separate shells, the buds, case body, lid and hinge, so the case can stand open with the buds seated. Generic over-ear headphones model the headband, sliding yokes, rotating cups and compressible pads as separate parts. The pair can be worn, hung on a stand or set on a desk.

Speakers cover the stage and the living room. A passive PA speaker has the trapezoid cabinet, woofer and horn tweeter of a box driven by a separate amplifier, and a tripod stand with a telescoping pole lifts it above a crowd. A public address horn stays at 7,274 polygons so many copies can line a wall. The red horn tower explains its own shape: the flare matches the driver to the air, so a horn needs a fraction of the power a conventional box does. Soundbars with subwoofers sit under wall-mounted televisions.

Display pieces help retail scenes, from headphones on a mannequin bust to a simple earbud box of 123 polygons. In the wider Electronics & Gadgets catalog, this is the shelf for product renders, home and studio interiors, store displays, event stages and unboxing shots.

weapons/rifles.lead: Rifles and carbines from the world wars to modern modular designs: Soviet-pattern rifles with wooden and polymer furniture, American service rifles with carry handles, bullpup rifles of several European designs, a marksman rifle and an amphibious rifle. Scopes, a thermal sight, a butt plate, an open rifle case and a remote weapon station for vehicle roofs complete the section.
body: On a rifle the furniture is the identification, so the models here spend their detail on stocks, handguards and finishes. A Soviet-pattern rifle of 47,230 polygons models the side-folding plum polymer stock, the muzzle brake ports and the gas block. Eight maps carry the polymer, the phosphate finish and the wear along the handguard. A British bullpup service rifle with its magazine behind the grip is built entirely from quads, with seven maps for the matte finish, worn edges and lens coating. An infantry rifle carried through both world wars threads its sling through slots in the stock rather than swivels.

Older and specialized patterns sit alongside. A Soviet semi-automatic carbine keeps its wooden stock and folding bayonet in 20,098 polygons. A marksman rifle shows a skeleton stock and slotted wooden handguards, and a French bullpup carries its long handle and folding bipod. Separate parts serve restoration and armory scenes: a scope on a quick-detach mount with adjustment turrets, a metal butt plate with screw recesses, and a sand-colored hard case with foam lining.

Parts are modeled in place rather than rigged, and many rifles in this Weapons subcategory hold CheckMate Pro certification. The models are intended for film and television props, games, simulation and training, museum displays and history education, where an accurate silhouette and period finish matter most.

weapons/pistols.lead: Handguns and the gear around them: classic double-action revolvers, western gun belts, modern service pistols with polymer frames and a large-frame semi-automatic. Soviet-era service and automatic pistols, a match air pistol, a revolving shotgun and a flare pistol add range. Belt and thigh holsters, hard transport cases and foam-lined pistol cases make up a large share of the section.
body: The revolver with a fluted cylinder, long barrel and curved grip under an exposed hammer is the shape most people picture for a western or a detective story. A second build shows every chamber loaded. Leather gear follows the same period, with a western gun belt carrying cartridge loops, tooled leather and a low-slung holster. A compact Soviet service pistol uses ten maps for blued steel, worn edges and the dark plastic grip. A match air pistol looks nothing like a service weapon, with a molded orthopedic grip, a compressed air cylinder around the barrel and sights on a long rail.

Holsters are modeled as objects worth a close-up. A belt holster takes its shape from the weapon it is molded around, so the trigger guard bulge, the muzzle end, the retention strap and the belt loops are all there in 4,784 quads. A drop-leg holster rides on the thigh with a flat platform, a retention hood and straps with quick-release buckles. It is static, since a holster needs no rig. Cases range from a hard locking box with padlock eyes to a flare pistol case with its rounds as separate pieces.

A revolving shotgun with StemCell materials keeps its polymer, bluing and wear consistent between offline and real-time renders. Within Weapons, this subcategory leans toward the prop table: film and television, westerns and crime drama, games, training and museum displays.

weapons/missiles-rockets.lead: Missiles and rockets as hardware for documentaries, museums, games and simulation: anti-ship and air-launched cruise missiles, ballistic and interceptor missiles, shoulder-launched systems with their sights and tripods, and rocket-propelled grenade rounds. Launch equipment fills the rest, from deck canister launchers to truck and tracked air defense launchers and a missile on its transporter trailer.
body: Most missiles are bodies of revolution, so faceting on a nose cone shows at once. One surface-to-air missile is built with subdivision geometry for that reason, with the fins, booster seam and seeker section modeled. A naval deck launcher is a set of angled canisters bolted to the deck and deliberately nothing more, textured with 24 maps at 4096 x 4096. An air-launched hypersonic weapon is mostly booster: a rocket stage accelerates it, then a wedge-shaped glide body separates. A shoulder-launched anti-tank set of 199,825 polygons includes the launch tube, command unit, sight, tripod and the missile itself.

Polygon budgets follow how the hardware is seen. A stealthy air-launched cruise missile stays at 10,352 polygons because it is almost always shown in multiples under a wing, and a game-ready anti-ship missile needs only 3,093. A rocket grenade round is built from 3,856 clean quads. At the heavy end, a long-nose tractor hauling a strategic missile on a transporter trailer reaches 2,012,610 polygons, and truck-mounted and tracked air defense launchers raise their canisters.

Like the rest of the Weapons category, the section is meant for neutral, factual use: defense and history documentaries, museum and exhibition displays, news graphics, simulation and training, film and games. CheckMate certification is common, and several pages carry extra versions of the same missile.

weapons/knives-swords.lead: Blades from many periods and cultures: Japanese katana, wakizashi and ninjato with lacquered scabbards, medieval arming swords, falchions, a Scottish claymore and two-handed swords, curved Arab swords, British and French officers' swords, and knives for hunting, diving and military service. Sheaths, a sword belt, a katana display rack and a kitchen sharpener sit alongside the blades.
body: The falchion is a sword shaped like a tool: weight forward, single-edged and closer to a cleaver than to a dueling blade. One version comes with its sheath in 13,066 quads and eight maps, and another shows polished steel with faint pitting near the edge and worn leather on the grip. The katana keeps its gentle curve, round guard and diamond pattern on the handle wrap, and a lacquered rack of five swords dresses a dojo or a collector's room. The claymore's forward-sloping quillons end in quatrefoils, and the British officer's sword has a pierced steel basket hilt with a wire grip sized for a gloved hand.

Most blades are light, which suits crowds and games: a Viking sword with a lobed pommel needs only 1,476 polygons, so dozens of warriors can share a scene. Knives are modeled around their working details. The dive knife has a serrated spine, a line cutter notch and a metal butt for tapping on tanks. The hunting karambit locks into the hand with a finger ring, and a Soviet sawback bayonet is game ready. A Second World War fighting knife pairs a clip-point blade with a stacked leather washer handle.

Leather pieces range from a stitched knife sheath with a snap strap to a sword belt with ten maps for worn leather and brass fittings. Historical film and theater, martial arts and samurai scenes, fantasy games and museum cases are the natural settings for this Weapons subcategory.

furniture-interior/chairs.lead: Seating for every kind of room: office and meeting chairs, armchairs and bean bags, dining sets, bar and loft stools, school desks and baby high chairs. Salon and doctor's chairs, director's and camping chairs and a lifeguard chair cover working settings. Throne chairs in gilded, black and red velvet versions suit palace, fantasy and holiday scenes.
body: Good seating shows how it carries weight. The camping chair is built open with the fabric tensioned over the frame, since the sag of a cloth sling on tubes is what makes it look sittable. Nine maps carry the polyester, the powder-coated tubing and the plastic feet. The director's chair crosses its wooden frame in an X under a canvas sling, in tall and standard versions. The school desk and chair, 9,157 quads, keeps the pencil groove and the book shelf under the seat, the details that make it school furniture.

Many chairs are meant to be repeated. A steel-frame meeting chair stays at 10,084 polygons for rows of seating, and a loft metal stool of 4,837 polygons can line a whole bar counter. Specialist pieces fill particular rooms. A salon wash station pairs a ceramic basin and chrome faucet with a reclining chair, and a white doctor's stool rolls on casters. A wooden high chair with a removable tray stays light enough for real-time nursery scenes.

The thrones are the showpieces: a carved chair with lion-paw feet, scrolled armrests and tufted upholstery, and a red velvet seat for a mall Santa. Within Furniture & Interior, this subcategory furnishes architectural interiors, office and restaurant plans, salons, clinics, film sets and games.

furniture-interior/tables.lead: Tables for homes, offices, classrooms and the outdoors: dining tables laid for a meal, rustic farmhouse and carved arabesque dining groups, reception desks, drafting and library tables. Folding, picnic and camp tables, patio side tables, a low floor table and a rolling overbed desk cover everyday use. A sci-fi command desk and a carved partners desk modeled after a famous presidential desk suit film sets.
body: Set tables carry most of the detail. A round banquet table for eight spends nearly all of its 209,579 polygons on the tableware, with every fork, flute and folded napkin modeled beside a flower vase. A low wooden table set for Arabian tea service holds an engraved long-spouted kettle and small glass cups. A vintage dining group repeats arabesque carving across the aprons, turned legs and openwork chair backs. The architect's drafting table tilts its wooden top on crank mechanisms beside a tall swivel stool.

Reception desks show two approaches. A classic curved counter with paneled fronts and molded trim fits hotel lobbies, law offices and clinics. A high-tech counter with a raised transaction ledge and a recessed light strip needs only 8,899 polygons. For rooms filled with copies, the square library table stays at 7,856 polygons, the classroom table is built for many identical units, and a green plastic patio table can repeat across a beach bar.

Outdoor and home pieces complete the Furniture & Interior tables. There is an all-quad picnic table with attached benches, a folding aluminum picnic table, a white event table with fold-flat legs and a sun lounger with a side table. Indoors, a TV tray holds dinner in front of the sofa, and a low floor table follows the tea rooms of Japan and Korea.

furniture-interior/beds.lead: Beds and sleeping places for homes, hospitals, barracks and campsites, from family bedrooms to field shelters. The range covers dressed double and queen beds, wooden cribs, children's bunks, steel barracks bunks, hospital beds and neonatal rooms, camp cots and inflatable mattresses. A few pieces show the moments around sleep, such as breakfast trays and children tucked under the covers.
body: Home bedrooms start with fully dressed beds that need no extra props. Queen Bed 3 arrives with mattress, linens and pillows, and its 36,974 polygons go into duvet folds, pillow seams and rounded frame corners. The Lifting Bed with Storage Function adds a gas-lift base that raises the platform over a large storage box. For nurseries, the Wooden Infant Bed is a slatted crib in 17,902 polygons. The Two Story Children's Bed brings a ladder, safety rails and storage below.

Institutional beds form a second large group. The Military Bunk Bed Worn stacks two steel berths with chipped paint and sagging mattresses in 168,728 polygons. That density keeps the rounded tubing smooth in close views. The Metal Bunk Beds Set and the Army Single Bed with Bedding furnish barracks, hostels and field hospitals. For medical scenes there is a single-bed patient room, a neonatal room with clear bassinets and monitors, and a hospital bed whose head and knee sections fold. Complete rooms are far heavier than single beds, since walls, furniture and fittings come together.

Most beds are static, and many carry CheckMate Pro certification. The black leather beauty treatment bed is rigged, so its backrest and leg section can move, and one sleeping little girl has groomed fur hair. The quilted Double Size Sleeping Mattress, 6,168 polygons with StemCell certification, fits games and real-time interiors. Dressed beds and finished rooms serve architectural visualization, hotel renders and medical training material across the furniture and interior catalog.

furniture-interior/cabinets-storage.lead: Cabinets, shelves and storage units for homes, shops, hospitals and workshops. The section holds kitchen and nursery wall shelves, bookcases, TV cabinets and vanities, supermarket gondolas, pharmacy racks, steel garage cabinets and warehouse shelving. Some arrive empty and ready for your own props, others come already stocked with books, medicine boxes or makeup.
body: Retail and storage scenes are covered from the aisle to the back room. The Retail Store Display Shelving is an empty supermarket gondola with adjustable shelves on a slotted back panel. At 13,884 polygons it is light enough to build whole aisles from repeats. The stainless steel Standing Shelving Unit needs only 4,848 polygons for its wire shelves and corner posts. When shelves should look full from the start, the Pharmacy Shelf Unit with Products models every box, bottle and tube separately in 469,798 polygons.

Home furniture runs from a 1,286-polygon kitchen shelf to the Modern TV Cabinet, whose 332,286 polygons give it rounded edges and fine panel seams. The Wood Bookcase with Ladder has molded cornices and a rolling ladder hooked to a top rail. The Bookcase with Books fills every shelf with volumes of varied heights and leaning angles. The Elegant White Vanity Dresser stands on cabriole legs under a tall framed mirror, its top set with lipsticks, compacts and perfume bottles.

Several pieces serve specialized rooms. Hospital bassinet carriers come with drawers and lower shelves, and a blue endoscope drying cabinet carries StemCell certification. A salon shampoo station joins a tilting basin to a cabinet, and a gray steel wall cabinet hangs above a garage workbench. The units are static, so doors and drawers stay modeled in place. Interior designers, store planners and game artists can furnish a room or a whole shop floor from this part of furniture and interior.

nature-plants/trees.lead: Trees modeled leaf by leaf and branch by branch, from oaks in summer and winter to flowering cherries and fruit trees. Date and coconut palms, mangroves on stilt roots, cypresses and podocarpus cover warmer climates. Smaller pieces include bare and spooky trees, single branches, banana leaves, pine cones and a low poly oak for forests.
body: Many trees here are heavy by design, because leaves and needles are real geometry rather than flat cards. The Red Oak Old Tree Summer reaches 1,450,047 polygons, with tens of thousands of separate leaves that let the canopy read correctly from below. The Flowering Cherry Tree packs its blossom in dense clusters along the branches, so it passes as sakura where generic trees fail. The Red Oak Old Tree Winter takes the opposite route. Its 275,063 polygons are all branch, and the taper and forking of each limb carry the silhouette.

Fruit trees suit gardens, orchards and courtyards. The Orange Tree with Fruits models every leaf and orange, and the Cherry Tree with Cherries hangs ripe fruit in clusters that hold up in close shots. The Mangrove Tree Shrub and the Mangrove Trees group stand on arched stilt roots for tropical coasts and river deltas. The Green Pine Branch spends 396,500 polygons on needles built as geometry, with eighteen texture maps for needles, bark and resin.

Choosing a tree mostly means choosing a polygon budget. Hero trees for film, architectural visualization and close renders run into the millions. The Lowpoly Red Oak Forest Tree uses 2,579 polygons, so a game forest can hold hundreds of them. The Round Soil Ground Cross Section with Tree Fur cuts a disc of earth to show roots and soil layers for science and education visuals. Within nature and plants, this subcategory sits next to flowers and terrain, and many of its trees carry StemCell or CheckMate certification.

nature-plants/flowers.lead: Flower 3D models from a single orchid stem to a whole meadow. Orchids, plumeria, freesia, magnolia, camellia, poppies, chamomile, jasmine, spider lilies and bird of paradise blooms sit beside bouquets, vases, a planter box and a flowering bonsai. Many blooms build their petals as real geometry, so they keep their shape in close shots.
body: Orchids appear in several forms, from single stems to finished arrangements. The Orchid Flower is a single stem in 2,358 polygons, all quads, light enough to repeat across a hotel lobby or a spa counter. Orchid 3 lets thick aerial roots spill over the pot rim, and the Orchid Stem and Black Vase is a minimal arrangement for modern interiors. The Plumeria Exotic Flower stays at 2,000 polygons, so a whole lei can be threaded from copies without slowing the scene.

Several sets follow a plant through time. Stages of Poppy Flower Growth runs from a closed hairy bud to an open red flower and a seed head in 224,223 polygons. Tomatoes Fruits and Flowers shows fruit at different ripening stages beside the yellow flowers. That pairing is botanically correct and makes a greenhouse scene look alive. The Bouquet of Chamomile Flowers spends most of its 77,832 polygons on finely divided, almost thread-like foliage that cards cannot fake.

Larger pieces set the stage. The Meadow with Blooming Flowers covers foregrounds with grass, blossoms and scattered stones, and the Orange Tree with Flowers models every leaf and petal in 2,004,775 polygons. The Miniature Bonsai Tree with Flowers in Pot uses fur for its dense crown, while the corpse flower model stands taller than a visitor. Many single blooms are StemCell certified. In nature and plants, these flowers end up in cosmetics and perfume product shots, spa and wedding visuals, botany lessons and garden visualization.

nature-plants/rocks-terrain.lead: Rocks, stones and pieces of landscape, from a polished sea stone to forest cliffs built as hero landmarks. The section holds pebbles, river rocks and boulder sets, along with coal, amber and grill lava rocks. Desert buttes, a Mount Fuji relief, a gabion basket and floating islands for fantasy skies complete it.
body: Much of the section is light scatter. The White Sea Stone takes just 419 polygons for a wave-polished oval, and Stone 5 is a low pebble in 982 quads. Stone 2 is a rounded gray river rock that subdivides without pinching. These small rocks keep a simple outline and let their textures carry cracks, grain and pitting. Sets save placement time: the Field Stone Set lines a path with rough boulders in 3,840 polygons. The Boulder Stone Set brings weathered rocks for riverbanks and rugged game terrain.

Landmarks and terrain sit at the other end. The Mitten Buttes and Merrick Butte formations from Monument Valley are spare meshes meant for distant desert panoramas. The Topographic Terrain Model of Mount Fuji shows the volcanic cone, the summit crater and the foothills as a tabletop relief map. Fantasy scenes get floating islands at several weights. The Soaring Highland Rock needs 7,417 polygons and has a flat plateau for a castle or shrine. The Levitating Forest Rock and Soaring Forest Cliff run to tens of millions of polygons.

Some models are rock props rather than landscape. There is a Black Coal Rock for mine carts and stove scuttles, porous Grill Lava Rocks and an Amber Stone of fossil resin. A Gabion Square Basket packs stones into a wire cage for retaining walls and garden borders. Level designers, matte painters, landscape architects and geography teachers all find material in this corner of nature and plants.

industrial-equipment/cranes.lead: Cranes for construction sites, ports and factories, many of them posed at work with a load on the hook. Tower and luffing jib cranes, crawler and ring cranes, all-terrain mobile and spider mini cranes stand beside ship-to-shore container cranes, harbor portal cranes and workshop hoists. Loads include concrete slabs, pour buckets, bulk bags and shipping containers.
body: Tower cranes are the tallest structures here, and their weight sits in the lattice. The Construction Tower Crane uses 1,287,576 polygons, mostly in the triangulated truss sections of mast and jib. The Tower Crane 3D Model balances a long jib against a counter jib stacked with concrete blocks. The Heavy Lifting Ringer Crane spends 599,443 polygons on a ring track, an A-frame mast, ballast trays and thousands of lattice members.

Mobile cranes cover city lifts and tight sites. Compact Mobile Crane 2 models the telescopic boom, hook block, outrigger pads and operator cab. The Spider Mini Crane Unfolded Position spreads its legs wide on rubber tracks. Scenes with a load save staging work, as in the Mobile Crane With Concrete Slab lifting a precast panel. A truck-mounted knuckle boom crane holds a concrete skip with its operator at the controls. In the Lifting Crane with 1 Ton Bulk Bag, the woven bag sags believably between its loops.

Port cranes include a red ship-to-shore crane holding a container above the quay and a yellow level luffing crane on a rail-mounted portal. Some models are rigged, among them the Compact Mobile Crane Generic Rigged and a harbor crane whose red lattice boom can slew and lift. Static versions suit architectural visualization and construction marketing, and rigged ones help with logistics animation, training and simulation. Smaller lifting gear, such as an electric chain hoist on a beam trolley, completes the crane range within industrial equipment.

industrial-equipment/tractors-agricultur.lead: Farm machinery and the tools that came before it. Utility tractors, tractors with tipper and dump trailers, combine harvesters, rice, beet and grape harvesters, hay rakes, balers, a potato planter and a lawn tractor make up the core. History reaches back to an antique hand plow and an ancient Egyptian wooden plow, while a driverless tractor points ahead.
body: Many models show machines the way they work in the field, coupled to an implement. The Tractor with Body Tipper Trailer is a subdivision model of 423,526 polygons, so its tires and cab curves smooth cleanly. Tractor with Used Twin Rotary Rake Generic tows a double rotor hay rake with folding arms. A mud-streaked tractor pulls a grain cart with a folding unloading auger. One scene pairs a red combine with a tractor and an open grain trailer, the usual convoy of a harvest day.

Harvesters change shape with the crop they gather. The Combine Harvester Generic shows a machine that cuts, threshes and separates in one pass. Its wide header, body of drums and sieves, grain tank and swinging auger all follow from that job. A tracked rice combine is narrow and set low for flooded paddies, and a straddle grape harvester drives over vineyard rows. A three-axle beet harvester lifts, cleans and stores sugar beets, and a combine with a corn header comes dirty from a working day.

For history lessons and museum scenes, the Old Hand Plow keeps its worn handles and rusty moldboard in 43,584 polygons. The Ancient Egyptian Wooden Plow recreates the scratch plow of the Nile valley. The Self-Driving Drone Tractor has no cab at all, only sensors, cameras and deep tire lugs. A terminal tractor for trailer yards and a wheeled scraper for earthworks also belong to this industrial equipment subcategory. Static throughout, these machines fit farming games, machinery brochures, documentaries and rural visualization.

industrial-equipment/robots-automation.lead: Robot arms and automated machines for factories, hospitals, warehouses and farms. Six-axis industrial arms run from compact to heavy payload, joined by collaborative robots, grippers, surgical systems, warehouse drive units and a pallet wrapper. Field robots work crop rows, a service robot brings food to restaurant tables, and a few pieces reach into orbit and science fiction.
body: Industrial arms come in several sizes, each matched to a different job. The Generic Industrial Robot is a compact six-axis arm on a round base for small parts assembly and packaging. Its motor covers, wrist joint and tool flange take 69,130 polygons. Mid range arms are the workhorses that fit in a cell beside a machine tool. Heavy-payload arms add bulky turning bases, rear counterweights and long reaching booms. The Robot Two Finger Gripper has parallel jaws and a flange that bolts onto an arm. The Compact Collaborative Robot shares an assembly bench with people, with no safety cage needed.

Medical robotics has its own corner in the section. A four-arm surgical robotic system shows long jointed booms converging over the patient, and a second version adds the surgeon console and an operating table. Service and logistics robots are lighter still. The Restaurant Delivery Robot Waiter needs 15,637 polygons for a rounded column, open trays and a screen face. The Automated Warehouse Robot Generic slides under shelving pods in just 13,386 polygons.

Rigging is rare here; one example is an orange arm with a two-finger gripper whose joints rotate for pick-and-place animation. The robotic arm of the International Space Station and the Sci-Fi Manipulator Arm with hydraulic pistons carry the section into orbital and fiction scenes. Factory planners, automation vendors, medtech and agritech teams and engineering teachers can all use these industrial equipment models for presentations and demos.

industrial-equipment/forklifts-loaders.lead: Lifting and earthmoving machines for warehouses and building sites. Counterbalance forklifts, telescopic handlers, wheel loaders, compact track and skid steer loaders and tracked and wheeled excavators sit beside separate buckets, tracks and boom assemblies. Several machines come loaded with bricks, boxes or a stretch-wrapped pallet, and a few carry an operator or an auger.
body: Forklifts cover warehouse and dock scenes. One counterbalance forklift spends 445,942 polygons on the mast channels, carriage, forks, overhead guard and counterweight. The mast gets the most care, since it is the part a viewer checks first. Other versions carry a plastic pallet, a wooden pallet or a full stack of red bricks with every brick modeled. The Military Forklift is a rough terrain truck with big lugged tires and a protected cab. A heavy-duty blue forklift lifts a stretch-wrapped pallet of cartons.

Loaders and excavators fill construction sites. The Generic Front End Loader puts 465,069 polygons into the bucket, lift arms, hydraulic rams and tire tread. Forty texture maps cover its yellow paint, chipped edges and dirt. Telescopic handlers lift pallets onto roofs and scaffolds, and compact track loaders work landscaping jobs on rubber tracks. The Skid Steer Loader with Operator comes with a seated worker at the controls. The Open Pit Mining Dragline Excavator, a simplified build, dwarfs trucks and workers at the edge of a pit.

Machine parts are offered as their own models. An Excavator Bucket with replaceable teeth takes 14,070 polygons, and an Excavator Track models every link pin and plate bolt. The Excavator Boom and Arm is rigged for digging animation. Some complete machines in this part of industrial equipment are rigged as well, and many carry CheckMate certification. Beyond still renders, they work in construction marketing, logistics training, simulators and game levels.

ships/boats-yachts.lead: Small craft and pleasure boats for marinas, rivers and lakes. Sailing yachts with full rigging, motor yachts with flybridges, wooden rowboats and runabouts, a pontoon boat, dive and fishing boats and a pedal boat sit together here. River push boats with barges, ferries and a traditional Gulf dhow follow, and some come staged with a pier, a trailer or a boarding dock.
body: Sailing yachts carry their rigging as real geometry, so the mast never looks unsupported. Offshore Sailing Yacht 2 spends 174,629 polygons on hull, winches, sails and cockpit. Twenty texture maps cover its gelcoat, teak, sailcloth and stainless fittings. The larger Sailing Yacht reaches 774,423 polygons with furled sails and a teak deck. Small Sailing Yacht 2 Sail Down rests at a mooring with its canvas packed along the boom. The Motor Yacht 3D Model follows the sheer line of the hull in 94,206 polygons, with flybridge, railings and swim platform modeled.

Working and passenger craft add variety. The Push Boat Ship has a tall stacked wheelhouse for seeing over a train of barges, and a second version comes with a pontoon barge attached. A double-deck harbor ferry can be placed alone or tied up at a wooden pier with water around it. A London river bus catamaran carries commuters in a low enclosed cabin. The Qatar Traditional Boat is a dhow with a raked stem, a wide transom and a single lateen sail.

Leisure scenes can draw on wooden rowboats with overlapping planks and oarlocks, a varnished runabout with chrome trim and a two-seat pedal boat. A dive boat with tank racks suits reef trips, and a rusty Second World War landing craft fits history projects. Resort and lake house renders, travel advertising, film sets and open-water game levels all use boats like these. Larger vessels have their own subcategories elsewhere in the ships category.

ships/submarines.lead: Submarines and submersibles for naval, research and tourism scenes. Nuclear ballistic missile and attack submarines and diesel-electric boats share the section with rescue submersibles and chambers. Tourist and private subs with large viewports, an unmanned submarine drone, a museum boat on concrete blocks and a bronze steampunk design complete it.
body: Military hulls are presented in neutral, documentary detail. A ballistic missile submarine is told apart by the long deck or raised hump behind the sail, where the missile compartment sits. One Soviet-era boat of the largest submarine type ever built needs only 36,355 polygons, leaving its broad smooth hull to the textures. Attack submarines trade that hump for a teardrop hull shaped for quiet running. One Russian model of this kind stays at 11,883 polygons. Light hulls like these let a whole fleet fit into a real-time naval scene.

Rescue and research craft form a second group. The Submarine Rescue Chamber is a deep-sea bell that mates with a stricken hatch and lifts the crew back to the surface. A rescue submersible sits on its launch and recovery cradle with the mating skirt underneath. The Tourist Submarine Mark V has rows of round viewports for reef watching. The Tourist Deep Sea Submarine seats passengers behind a large acrylic bubble. Old Yellow Submarine is a weathered research sub whose clean unwrap keeps rust streaks and peeling paint sharp.

Fiction and history round out the subcategory. The Fantasy Steampunk Submarine Bronze spends 270,985 polygons on rivets, pipes and fins, styled more like a storybook toy than a warship. A Second World War fleet submarine rests on concrete blocks the way museum boats are shown. That pose exposes the hull that normally stays below the waterline. Documentary makers, museum designers, defense educators and underwater film crews are the natural audience for this part of the ships category.

ships/naval-ships.lead: Warships and naval vessels for documentaries, simulation and film. Aircraft carriers with ski-jump or flat flight decks, amphibious assault ships, cruisers, destroyers, stealth frigates, corvettes and littoral combat ships are joined by a Second World War battleship. A three-masted sailing frigate and a few large civilian ships, such as a gas carrier, complete the section.
body: Modern surface combatants are defined by their silhouettes, and these models keep them readable. Cruisers carry blocky forward and aft deckhouses with flat phased-array radar panels. Frigates show clean, faceted surfaces shaped to reduce radar returns. A tumblehome stealth destroyer needs only 77,676 polygons, because its flat slab sides stay crisp with few faces. A trimaran littoral combat ship with a slender center hull sits beside a semi-planing steel design with a broad flight deck aft.

Carriers are among the heaviest models here. One nuclear-powered supercarrier reaches 2,144,989 polygons, down to catapult tracks, deck elevators and the radar arrays on its island. A Russian carrier shows its ski-jump bow and angled deck. The Military Aircraft Carrier Sea Vehicle Gray Simplified is reduced for scenes where a whole fleet is in view, yet still holds a detailed deck and island. An amphibious assault ship adds a full-length flight deck with two deck-edge elevators.

History and civilian shipping complete the picture. The Three Masted Heavy Frigate Raised Sails models every billowing sail, rigging line and cannon port in 1,227,764 polygons. The largest battleship of the Second World War appears afloat with its triple main turrets raised. The Gas Carrier Ship is recognizable by the domed pressure tanks on its deck, and a heavy load carrier rides low with a complete drilling rig on board. Naval history documentaries, museum exhibits, defense education, strategy games and fleet simulators draw on this subcategory of ships.

lighting/lamps.lead: Lamps for homes, offices, studios and period sets. Desk and table lamps, floor lamps with one or three shades, pendants, recessed ceiling fittings and bare-bulb sockets cover everyday rooms. A photo studio halogen stand, a camping lantern, a brass carbide miner's lamp, a searchlight-style tripod lamp and a medieval candle chandelier serve more particular scenes.
body: Reading and work lights make up the core. The Desk Lamp Blue has a jointed arm and a dome shade, with 29,981 polygons in the arm joints, hinge screws and weighted base. The Brown Leather Table Lamp shows stitched leather seams under a tapered shade. For living rooms, the Wood Floor Lamp pairs turned wooden legs with a fabric drum shade. The Floor Lamp with Three Shades Metal rounds off its conical shades in 112,517 polygons.

Ceiling and wall fittings are built to repeat. The Modern Hanging Pendant Lamp needs only 1,756 polygons, so a row of them over a kitchen island costs little. The Recessed Modular Ceiling Lamp White fills office and store ceilings with a grid of light cells. The Classroom Lamp is a bare batten in a reflector housing that instantly reads as a school or corridor. Loft interiors can use the Vintage Bronze Lamp Holder with Light Bulb or a black wall socket holding a bare filament bulb.

Some pieces belong to particular scenes. The Theater Nautical Lamp stands on a black tripod, a yellow railway warning lamp clamps to the rail head, and a switched-on salt lamp warms spa interiors. The Hanging Medieval Chandelier shows wax drips running down its candles. One backlight lamp is prepared as a closed, watertight shell for 3D printing. Lamps here dress rooms in interior visualization, furniture catalogs, film sets and game levels, while bulbs have their own subcategory under lighting.

lighting/bulbs.lead: Light bulbs and small light sources, from classic pear-shaped incandescent bulbs to smart LED bulbs and fluorescent tubes. Vintage filament bulbs come in globe, teardrop, tube and diamond shapes. Spot and flood reflectors, a car headlight bulb, LED tape, track heads, studio panels, warning beacons, sockets, string lights and a bulb-shaped speaker round out the group.
body: The classic bulb comes in both states, dark and lit. Electric Light Bulb keeps a clear glass envelope, a coiled filament on its supports and a threaded base in 7,538 polygons. Electric Light Bulb Illuminated shows the same shape with the filament glowing. The Electric Light Bulb Set gathers pear, globe and candle bulbs with filaments and support wires modeled inside the glass. Close-ups therefore glow convincingly once emission is applied. One vintage globe bulb even comes covered in a layer of dust.

Vintage filament bulbs suit lofts, cafes and patios. The shapes include a teardrop with a looping carbon filament, a large globe for bar counters, a slim tube with long strands and a faceted diamond envelope. The Vintage String Light Bulb is the kind hung in rows over patios and wedding venues. Modern lighting is covered too. The Smart Light Bulb has a frosted dome at 2,904 polygons, light enough for every fixture in a house. A fluorescent tube uses 1,936 quads with bi-pin contacts.

Beyond household bulbs, the subcategory holds a car halogen headlight bulb with a quartz capsule and locking tabs. A rotating LED warning beacon, a flat grow light panel for indoor farms and LED panel lights on tripod stands follow. A large soft panel on a rolling stand fits film set scenes. Most of these are small, light meshes for architectural visualization, product renders, electrical training material and game interiors. Lamps and fixtures sit next door in the lighting category.

sports-recreation/balls.lead: Balls for team sports, racket games, fitness and play. Rugby, soccer, volleyball, baseball and cricket balls share the section with golf, tennis and field hockey balls, fitness and medicine balls and perforated plastic practice balls. Several models pair the ball with its gear, such as a glove, a bat, a courtside training basket or a bowling ball return.
body: Seams and surfaces are where these models spend their geometry. The Cricket Ball concentrates 52,448 quad polygons in the six rows of stitching around its equator. The Baseball Ball follows the figure-eight double seam exactly. Rugby Ball Generic puts its 32,316 polygons into the pebbled grip and raised seams. The Golf Ball Generic models the dimple pattern that keeps a ball flying, in an unbranded form. The Tennis Ball presses its seam line into the surface in 4,824 quads.

Lighter models suit crowds and scattered props. The Field Hockey Ball White uses just 128 polygons and relies on smoothing, so dozens can roll across a practice pitch. Subdivision brings it up to macro quality when needed. The Fitness Stability Ball Blue needs 788 polygons and the Dual Grip Medicine Ball 1,632, sized for gym interiors and mobile workout apps. Official League Baseball Ball 1920 recreates a period ball with darker hide and thick seams. A pixel-pattern soccer ball gives a pitch a retro video game look.

Sets and scenes save staging time. Baseball Glove And Ball and its vintage counterpart cradle a stitched ball in laced leather. A baseball bat with a wrapped grip lies beside its ball. The Training Ball Basket with Balls heaps practice balls, each with its own seams, into a wire cart. A Rugby Ball Set dresses a locker room without repetition. Broadcast designers, sporting goods retailers, game studios and physical education teachers will find their props in this sports and recreation subcategory.

sports-recreation/hockey.lead: Ice hockey and field hockey gear for rinks, locker rooms and sports stores. Helmets with cages and visors, goalie masks, gloves, pads, sticks, pucks and nets come alongside a full rink with boards and glass. A few lighter pieces cover air hockey, fan still lifes and a cartoon shooting target.
body: Protective equipment is modeled piece by piece. The Hockey Shoulder Pads have a hard chest plate, rounded shoulder caps and layered foam in 59,823 polygons. The Hockey Shin Pads pair segmented shells with knee cups and hook-and-loop calf straps. Hockey Gloves center on the stacked foam segments over the knuckles that flex around a stick. One helmet carries a full wire face cage for youth players, and the Ice Hockey Helmet with Visor Game Ready has a clear half visor.

Polygon budgets range widely across the gear. The Hockey Stick takes only 158 polygons and the Field Hockey Stick Green 535, so whole teams can carry them in a real-time game. Hockey Puck 3 uses 1,276 quads with a knurled rim that subdivides cleanly. The Hockey Net shapes its tubular frame, mesh bag and skirt in 8,580 polygons. The Ice Hockey Rink provides dasher boards, glass panels, goals, painted lines, benches and penalty boxes in a single model.

Full kits and novelty props round things off. Hockey Equipment Generic 5 gathers helmet, gloves, pads, stick and skates, and a padded glove giving a thumbs-up suits match day graphics. A fan scarf with fur knit lies beside a goalie mask and pucks. A folding goal with a backstop serves driveway practice. On screen, this gear from sports and recreation shows up in broadcast design, sporting goods catalogs, sports games and coaching material.

sports-recreation/fitness-gym.lead: Gym equipment from a single dumbbell to a fully fitted hall. Kettlebells, dumbbells, weight plates, barbells, power cages and half racks cover strength training. Treadmills, a multi-station home gym, a fitness trampoline, stability and medicine balls, resistance bands and hand grippers cover the rest. A fitness tracker wristband joins the heavier gear for workout app and wearable scenes.
body: Free weights are light and easy to repeat. The Dumbbell Weight 10 LB has hexagonal heads that stop it rolling and needs only 220 polygons. Kettlebell 2 is a cast iron bell in 368 quads, and vinyl coated kettlebells come in several weights with flat bases and wide handles. The Dumbbell Weights Set adds knurled grips and plates locked by collars, with twelve texture maps for chrome bars and the fine crosshatch of the grip. A whole rack built from these costs very little to render.

Racks and machines carry more detail. Barbell and Plates 2 spends most of its 194,552 polygons on knurling, plate lettering and locking collars. The Power Cage Black and Barbell models upright posts, J-hooks, safety bars and a pull-up handle. A half rack with a loaded bar keeps its UVs free of overlaps, leaving room for powder coat colors and chalk dust. One treadmill uses 35 texture maps, so the console graphics, belt surface and painted frame each get their own material.

For a complete scene, the High-tech Gym fills a modern hall with treadmills, cable stations, rowing machines and weight racks. Each machine has its own frames, pulleys and consoles. The Multi Fitness Equipment Home Gym covers a full workout with a weight stack, padded bench and press arms. In sports and recreation, this is the equipment for fitness club design, workout videos, app illustrations and gym levels in games.

sports-recreation/camping-outdoor.lead: Tents and gear for campsites, hikes and field camps. Dome and family tents, canvas ridge tents, military and medical field tents and a tent pitched on a pickup bed form the core. Sleeping bags, camp cookware, a coffee pot and stove, tent stakes and packed parachutes complete the kit. Several tents come as sets, so a whole campsite builds quickly.
body: Tent fabric is shaped to look properly pitched. Camping Tent 2 pulls its fabric taut between crossed poles, with a rain fly, a vestibule and pegged guy lines, in 49,384 polygons. Vintage Camping Tent 2 is a canvas ridge tent with wooden poles and a rolled-back door flap. The Vintage Camping Tent Set lets the canvas sag slightly between poles, as if pitched by hand. The Camping Tents Set gathers shelters from a one-person dome to roomier family tents with porches.

Sleeping bags come rolled or laid out. The Folded Sleeping Bag shows the fiddly compressed roll with straps biting into the fabric, in 5,608 quads. Seven texture maps carry its ripstop nylon, webbing and buckles. The Deployed Sleeping Bag lies flat with puffy quilted channels and a folded collar, and the Warm Sleeping Bag has stitched baffles along a side zipper. A dome tent setup with a sleeping bag inside and a lantern by the entrance gives a ready night scene.

Camp cooking and field gear fill in the details. Camping Cookware nests pots, a frying pan and folding handles, and its textures add brushed aluminum, soot and scuffs. The blue enamel Camping Coffee Pot stays lean at 3,549 polygons, and a camping stove boils instant noodles on the flame. Military and medical field tents, a plastic tent stake and packed parachute rigs widen the range. Survival games, outdoor gear catalogs, adventure films and scouting lessons are where this sports and recreation gear tends to end up.

food-beverages/fruit-vegetables.lead: Fruit, vegetables and produce for kitchens, markets and gardens. Whole and sliced lemons, bananas, cherries, tomatoes, grapes and dates sit beside dragon fruit, granadilla, acerola and pomelo. Grape leaves, a tomato plant, a vegetable garden bed and a burlap sack of apples add growing and harvest scenes. A few models carry fruit into prepared food and bottled drinks.
body: Single fruits are built light so they can fill bowls and crates. The Cherry Fruit uses 192 polygons, the Lemon 475 and the Banana 1,118. The Unripe Tomato with Stem drops to 225, so a vine or a crate can carry dozens of them. The Tomato takes a different approach. Its slightly irregular sphere of 1,366 polygons carries ten texture maps for the waxy skin, its subsurface glow and the green calyx.

Cut fruit serves cocktails, nutrition graphics and recipe illustrations. The Lemon Round Slice needs just 580 polygons to float in a glass, and the Lemon Half keeps a perfectly flat cut face with a white pith ring. Green Grape Cross Section 2 opens a grape to show the flesh and seed pockets. The Granadilla Whole and Slice Fruit pairs a speckled orange shell with a half full of black seeds in translucent jelly. The Fresh Peeled Banana Cartoon offers a friendly stylized option for kids' content and games.

Living plants extend the subcategory. The Tomato Plant with Fruits and Flowers uses fur and dense foliage for a home garden canopy. The Vegetable Garden models individual leaves in planted rows, and Grape Leaves with Dew cut their serrated edges into geometry under beaded water. The Burlap Apple Sack Full Red Yellow sags under its load with fruit peeking out at the top. This produce from the food and beverages catalog turns up in grocery and packaging renders, cooking shows, nutrition lessons, farm games and film market scenes.

food-beverages/desserts-sweets.lead: Sweets and desserts for bakeries, cafes and party tables. Ice cream cones, scoops and tubs sit beside whole and crushed chocolate bars and layer cakes for birthdays and weddings. Donuts, eclairs, cookies, marshmallows, candy piles and a chocolate egg fill out the table. A liquid chocolate splash frozen in midair adds motion for packaging and advertising shots.
body: Ice cream models put their detail into texture. The Ice Cream Cone shapes a soft-serve swirl turn by turn and cuts the diamond waffle pattern into the geometry. Its ridges cast tiny shadows under a rim light. The Empty Ice Cream Cone waits for scoops, and the Vanilla Ice Cream Top can crown a cone, a cup or a sundae glass. For freezer shelves, the Ice Cream Pint Container needs 1,374 quads and has a lid that lifts off as its own object.

Chocolate appears in several states. The White Paper Wide Chocolate Bar holds the sharper creases of a paper wrapper. The Chocolate Bar sits half unwrapped over an engraved segment grid, and the crushed milk and dark bars show snapped squares, shards and crumbs. The Milk Chocolate Egg is about as light as a model gets, at 176 quad polygons. Cakes carry heavier detail than the bars. The Butter Cream Rose Flower Cake shapes the curled petals of each piped rose in 75,268 polygons, and the Vanilla Birthday Cake adds swirled icing, candles and sugar sprinkles.

Bakery and candy pieces fill a table quickly. The Pink Sprinkled Donut models each sprinkle as a separate piece, and the Colorful Candy Pile rounds every candy so highlights roll across the heap. A chocolate-glazed eclair sits beside a cup of coffee for a cafe break. One version of the ice cream cone is shaped as a single solid for 3D printing. Packaging designers, menu and ad photographers, food bloggers and game artists can stock a dessert table from this food and beverages subcategory.

food-beverages/drinks.lead: Drinks and their containers for bars, kitchens and packaging. Finished cocktails with ice and garnish, wine and beer bottles, beer mugs, kegs with taps, soda cans, juice jugs, takeaway coffee cups and coffee bags make up the range. A few pieces work as blank mockups for label artwork, and a coconut with a straw covers beach scenes.
body: Finished cocktails solve the hardest part of a drinks render, making ice and liquid sit together. The Mai Tai Cocktail arrives built in 30,125 quad polygons, with a layered pour, ice, straw and garnish. The Glass of Mojito Cocktail spends 79,823 polygons on individual ice chunks and muddled mint leaves, and its 22 maps include frosted condensation. A classic cocktail in a conical stemmed glass with green olives needs only 1,626 polygons.

Beer is covered from glass to bottle to keg. The Overflowing Beer Mug runs foam over the rim and down the side. Beer Bottle 2 gets the long neck, sharp shoulder and crimped crown cap right in 3,732 quads. The Beer Kegs Set and Beer Keg 50L model rolling rings and cut-out carry handles, and one keg comes with a picnic tap, a CO2 regulator and a hose. The Drink Soda Can with Water Droplets Red builds each droplet as geometry in 332,552 polygons for a chilled hero shot.

For packaging work, the Beer Keg with Tap and Label Mockup wraps a flat label band around its barrel. The Mockup Foil Coffee Bag is a blank pouch with a valve and folded top for testing artwork. Wine appears as single bottles with foil capsules and as a trio for still lifes, and coffee as a takeaway cup with a ribbed sleeve. With these models from food and beverages, a bar shelf, a packaging mockup or a film prop table can be dressed without modeling a single bottle.

containers-storage/boxes-crates.lead: Boxes, crates and packaging for warehouses, kitchens and takeaway counters. Wooden fruit and shipping crates, plastic milk and produce crates, pizza boxes, burger clamshells and noodle pails sit beside cartons, small containers, and gift and cake boxes. Several are built as clean packaging templates ready for your own artwork.
body: Wooden crates carry real construction. The Wooden Fruit Crate cuts the gaps between its slats as real openings in 6,330 quads. Light then falls through a stack in a way a textured solid box cannot reproduce. The Wooden Shipping Crate reads through its framing, with plank cladding, nail heads and corner braces in 17,324 polygons. Wooden Shipping Crate 3 models battens and plank seams as geometry for docks, warehouses and treasure rooms. A stack of weathered slat crates with loose boards around the base suits a barn.

Food packaging forms a second group. The Open Pizza Box and the Carton Pizza Box show folded flaps, rounded corners and a slightly warped lid. One version adds a fold-out carry handle, and a set of triangular slice boxes has clear windows. Chinese takeout pails come in two sizes with thin wire handles, and a brown paper burger box completes a food truck counter. Aseptic cartons with screw caps or straw holes keep folded seams sharp across flat panels. The Pint Milk Carton Generic Template serves dairy packaging mockups.

Plastic crates add an urban and market touch. The Milk Crate Plastic Black has a grid of square vents and molded handles. Portobello Mushrooms in Plastic Crate packs broad caps into a vented produce crate. Many of these models are light, so shelves and stacks stay fast in a scene. Packaging designers, retail and restaurant visualizers and warehouse level builders get a ready stock of containers from this containers and storage subcategory.

containers-storage/barrels-drums.lead: Barrels, drums and canisters for warehouses, taverns, yards and wastelands. Ribbed steel oil drums, wooden casks with iron hoops, plastic drums and water tanks, jerry cans and hazardous material barrels sit beside a cable drum and barrel stands. Several pieces turn drums into furniture or stage them with tires, rubble, forklifts and harvest props.
body: Steel drums cover industrial scenes in several conditions. A ribbed oil drum with a sealed lid and two bung caps needs only 5,142 polygons. The Heavy Damaged Crude Oil Barrel builds dented walls, a crushed rim and a torn seam into 8,392 polygons for decay and action scenes. The Radioactive Waste Barrels Set carries the yellow and black radiation trefoil. A gray containment drum with reinforced rings and lid bolts suits nuclear facility scenes. A drum cradle holds a barrel marked with a hazard diamond, the setup for tipping and dispensing chemicals.

Wooden barrels serve taverns, ships, wine cellars and medieval villages. The Wooden Barrel bulges at the belly in 10,110 polygons with a slightly recessed lid, and the Wood Barrel traces its staves and hoop edges more finely in 20,172. The Barrels Pyramid stacks casks for a saloon or harbor warehouse. The Tavern Barrel Stand holds several casks with taps on a timber cradle. A pumpkin on an old barrel beside a burlap sack gives a ready autumn vignette.

Plastic containers are lighter still. The Round Plastic Barrel 30 Gal is a blue polyethylene drum in 3,038 polygons. A double water storage unit joins two ribbed tanks with a connecting pipe, and a jerry can tips forward with a sculpted green stream pouring from its spout. Upcycled pieces turn drums into a bar table and an armchair whose ribs still run around the back. Under containers and storage, these barrels serve refinery and factory visualization, post-apocalyptic game levels, period films and loft interiors.

other/emoji.lead: Emoji turned into rounded 3D objects with the flat glossy look of the icons and real volume. Smiling, winking, laughing, worried, angry and star-eyed faces sit beside hand gestures such as thumbs up, clapping hands, a raised fist and pointing fingers. Hearts, flames, a party face, a clown, a robot, a devil and the smiling poop pile complete the set.
body: The challenge with an emoji in 3D is keeping it a symbol. The Thumbs Up Gesture Emoji gives the flat glyph a real hand shape in 625 polygons. It stops short of so much anatomy that it would no longer read as an icon. The Sign of the Horns Emoji keeps its rounded fingers clean from the front and from a three quarter angle, where flat icon geometry usually breaks. Index Pointing Up Emoji uses five maps matched to the flat cartoon shading, and its clean unwrap lets the yellow change to another skin tone.

Faces are smooth spheres with their features modeled rather than painted. The Devil Emoji shapes horns, a curled mouth and a heavy brow in 1,268 polygons. The Tears Of Joy Emoji has a wide grin and squeezed eyes, and the Party Face Emoji adds a cone hat, a noisemaker and confetti. The Flame Emoji is a dimensional object with flat emoji shading instead of a realistic fire. A volumetric flame in a row of icons would look like a mistake.

CheckMate Pro certification on many of the faces means consistent scale, so several emoji can stand in one row without one dominating. Light meshes like these spin and bounce smoothly in motion design. They drop into mobile games, sticker packs, social media graphics and explainer videos at almost no cost. The emoji live under the other category, alongside coins, stationery and small objects that fit no larger group.

other/coins-currency.lead: Coins, banknotes and money props for finance, history and crime scenes. US cents, dimes, half dollars and dollar coins share the section with Canadian, British, French and Chinese coins, an ancient Roman denarius and cryptocurrency tokens. Banknotes appear single, flying, stacked and piled, along with a money tree, counting machines and a briefcase packed with banded notes.
body: Coins are built with their relief in mind. The United States Coin Penny keeps the profile portrait and lettering in its maps, so 2,816 quads make a coin that stays tiny in memory. The US Half Dollar and US Silver Dollar give the reeded edge and raised rim real geometry. The Dime United States Coin adds six texture maps for its silvery tone and small wear marks. The French Euro Coin 20 Cent goes further, spending 34,187 polygons on the relief and the seven scalloped notches of its edge.

Paper money is modeled to bend. The 100 Dollar Bill curves gently instead of lying as a rigid card, and Flying Dollar Bills twists each note as if caught in midair. Larger props stage a scene in one placement. The Aluminum Case Full Of Money packs banded notes into an open briefcase in 2,096,426 polygons. The Mountain of 50 Euro Packs gives each bundle its own paper band, and Falling Dollar Bills from Money Tree drops notes from paper leaves. Two desktop counting machines come loaded with euro or dollar bills for bank teller scenes.

History and new money sit side by side. The Denarius Ancient Roman Silver Coin, a soldier's daily pay for a long time, needs only 1,140 polygons for museum and history projects. Gold and silver tokens stamped with cryptocurrency emblems serve finance news and explainers. Filed under the other category, these models suit banking and fintech visuals, numismatic catalogs, economics lessons, crime dramas and game loot.

other/stationery-office.lead: Desk and office objects for studies, classrooms and workplaces. Fountain, ballpoint and plastic pens, pencils, sharpeners and pencil shavings sit beside envelopes in several formats, clipboards, notebooks and journals. Binder clips, permanent markers and digital styluses for graphics tablets complete the desk, and most pieces are small, light props that hardly weigh down a scene.
body: Writing instruments carry their defining details. The Classic Fountain Pen spends 7,730 polygons on barrel, cap, clip and a nib with its breather hole and slit. The nib is the part that shows whether a pen is real or a prop. Writing tools are kept light: a steel ballpoint pen holds its clip and grip detail in 1,842 polygons, so a desk scene can carry several of them. The Transparent Plastic Ballpoint Pen shows its ink tube through a hexagonal barrel that stays crisp under refraction.

Paper items are built only as heavy as they need to be. White Envelope 2 is 330 polygons, a flat rectangle with a flap and a slight bulge where the contents sit. The White DL Envelope takes the long format for a sheet folded in three. The Open Journal with Fountain Pen lays a pen across cream pages, and the Paper Notebook with Pen keeps its page curl smooth near the lens. Clipboard 2 spends much of its 18,982 polygons on the spring clip and hinge, which show clearly in close-ups.

Classroom tools fill in the rest. The Hand Crank Pencil Sharpener clamps to a desk edge with a crank arm and a clear shavings drawer. A handheld plastic sharpener holds its steel blade with one screw, and Pencil Shavings gives each curled spiral a painted, ruffled rim. Colored Binder Clips and graphics tablet styluses with side buttons extend the set toward modern offices. Office and school interiors, product renders, education content and game environments are natural settings for these props from the other category.
